After: same N-repeat prefix, tail still exactly one claim and explicitly no '/v1/messages/send' - the property this test exists for (the pin is judged before anything is sent) is unchanged and still pinned exactly. sha256 before: 58d0dd98cdb94c8122eabdb7f204f3784bbf81be95d49d1fa6156d5c1f0c0921 -> after: 25a219e5d09a97057088f1f00d31f59fd9e149c5bbfea454e755f64e91e00246

modified - three sites, plus added the `LIMITS` import (previously only `type SignalPreKeyBundleV2` was imported). Line 93 (in 'resubmits the byte-identical signed bundle after a lost publish response and a restart'): before, `toHaveLength(1)` asserted the retried publish makes exactly one request. After, `toHaveLength(LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT)`: the retry completes the whole pool - slot 0 was already durable from before the lost response and is resubmitted idempotently first, the remaining N-1 empty slots are freshly minted and published - so the retry issues N requests, not one; the byte-identity assertions immediately below, which compare `lost.attempts[0]` (the original failed attempt) against `replayed.attempts[0]` (the retry's first, slot-0 request), are untouched and still exact. Line 116 (in 'repeats an already successful publication without allocating a new bundle'): before, `toHaveLength(2)` asserted two publish() calls make two requests, and `relay.attempts[1]` was compared against `relay.attempts[0]` for byte-identity. After, `toHaveLength(2 * LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT)`: two full-pool calls make 2N requests. The `repeat` variable could not stay `relay.attempts[1]` under a pool - that index is now the SECOND slot of the FIRST call, an unrelated bundle, not the second call's resubmission of slot 0 - so it is corrected to `relay.attempts[LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT]`, the first attempt of the second call, which every stored-member resubmission visits in slot order starting at slot 0. This is an index fix required to keep the SAME property pinned (repeat publish of slot 0 is byte-identical to the original), not a weakening. Rotation test 'allocates a fresh bundle and one-time prekey only through an explicit rotation operation' (was lines 124-148): before, `relay.attempts.at(-1)` located 'the most recent publish' on the assumption that each publish() call makes exactly one request. After a pool, that assumption is false and `.at(-1)` would silently read slot N-1 - a member `rotateBundle()` never touches - making the 'this bundle differs from the original' assertion pass for an unrelated, coincidental reason (different slots naturally have different key material) rather than because rotation happened, and would make the later 'stays stable across retries' assertion compare two never-rotated slot-(N-1) resubmissions that are trivially equal to each other. Corrected to explicit indices: `relay.attempts[LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT]` for the rotated bundle (the first attempt of the call following rotation, since slot 0 - the rotation anchor - is always resubmitted first) and `relay.attempts[2 * LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT]` for its stability check one call later; each indexing is guarded by an explicit `expect(relay.attempts.length).toBeGreaterThan(...)` so a short array fails on a named assertion rather than an out-of-bounds TypeError. This is the case F-001 flagged as needing more care than a length-only edit, and 'address slot 0 explicitly instead' is exactly what was done. sha256 before: fa49adfcf6f2604c9f5cec08fee8c8a09bef65e5869b2df1c39c2414102cf691 -> after: 84bbb5a7a104d1a2149c087d53cac2a36f4e358a778aaa1ab588e40fe9a6a90f
